$comment: A TRANSCRIPTION RECORD, not vendored source. Every row names where a value or a formula came from, what it means, what Global Idle decided about it, and where that decision is pinned - the format REFERENCES.md requires. No Canary code is copied into this repository; `probe` carries only the pattern that locates the value and the exact literal that was read, so the record can be re-verified against a real checkout.
verification: Point CANARY_SOURCE at a checkout of the repository above, at that commit, and the SRC cases re-run every probe against the real files. Without it they still assert that the authored content matches this record, which is what CI proves.

imports.observed: A Rat has 20 hit points.
Killing a Rat awards 5 experience.
A Rat's movement speed is 67.
imports.reason: Carried as presentation/pacing data. Phase 2 simulates no positions, so nothing reads it yet.

imports.observed: A Rat swings every 2000 ms.
A Rat's melee tops out at 8 damage; Canary stores damage dealt as a negative number.
imports.reason: The sign is Canary's convention for damage on a health delta, not part of the value. Global Idle stores the magnitude and subtracts it.

imports.observed: A Rat's defence value is 5, the input to the uniform_random(defense/2, defense) block roll.
A Rat's armour value is 1, which under blockHit means a flat --damage rather than a roll.
A Rat's authored mitigation is 0.07; Monster::getMitigation multiplies it by the defence multiplier (1.0) and the configurable monsterMitigationMultiplier (default 1.5) before use.
imports.reason: The configurable 1.5 is a server tunable, not creature data. It changes nothing Phase 2 can observe: for every integer damage below 953 the truncation in mitigateDamage lands on the same integer at 0.07 and at 0.105. SRC2 proves that over the whole range this phase can produce.

imports.observed: Gold drops with chance 100000 out of Canary's 100000 denominator: every kill.
imports.reason: Phase 2 has no loot table, no BaseItem and no ItemInstance (Phase 3 owns all three). The same entry is modelled as a CURRENCY reward, and the denominator is normalised to a probability.

imports.reason: Same adaptation as rat.gold.chance. The minimum is 1, which is Canary's implicit floor for a dropped stack.

Each piece of the pre-vocation leather kit is worth 1 armour.
Each piece of the pre-vocation leather kit is worth 1 armour.

imports.observed: Defence is ((defenseSkill / 4.0 + 2.23) * defenseValue * defenseFactor * scaling) * vocation->defenseMultiplier, truncated by the int32_t return.
imports.reason: Authored as a flat profile number because Phase 2 has no equipment to recompute it from. Both readings of the tutorial Character truncate to the same 4: unarmed (skill 10, value 7, scaling 0.15) gives 4.9665, and dagger-armed (sword skill 10, dagger defence 6, scaling 0.146) gives 4.14348. SRC4 computes both.

imports.reason: Modelled as charges on the combat profile: no item, no flask, no inventory. Phase 3 replaces it with real items.

imports.observed: Total experience required to BE a level.

probe.pattern: uint64_t Player::getExpForLevel\(const uint32_t level\) \{\s*\n\s*(return \(\(\(level - 6ULL\) \* level \+ 17ULL\) \* level - 12ULL\) / 6ULL \* 100ULL;)

imports.reason: Transcribed into bigint. The integer division is Canary's and is kept: an algebraic inverse would disagree by one exactly where a level-up happens.

imports.observed: The maximum a melee swing can roll.

probe.captured: return attackValue > 0 ? static_cast<int32_t>(std::round((0.085 * attackFactor * attackValue * attackSkill) + (level / 5))) : 0;

imports.reason: level / 5 is integer division on uint32_t, so it is Math.floor here.

imports.observed: An ARMED melee swing rolls normal_random(level / 5, maxDamage) — the floor is not zero.
imports.reason: Weapon::useFist rolls normal_random(0, maxDamage) instead. The tutorial profile is armed, so the armed floor applies; the two agree below Level 5 and diverge from Level 5 up.

imports.observed: Defence subtracts a uniform roll between half the defence value and the defence value.
Armour above 3 subtracts a uniform roll; armour of 1 to 3 subtracts exactly 1.
Mitigation subtracts a percentage and the int32_t assignment truncates, so any non-zero mitigation costs at least one point.
A normal distribution centred on 0.5 with sigma 0.25, rejection-sampled into [0, 1], then scaled onto [min, max] with lround.
imports.reason: The DISTRIBUTION is transcribed exactly; the SAMPLING METHOD is not. Rejection sampling consumes a variable number of draws, and this engine's replay contract requires a fixed one, so the same truncated normal is produced by inverse transform in a single draw. The entropy source is the Phase 0B seeded generator rather than std::mt19937, because a run must be reproducible from a durable seed.

imports.observed: A uniform integer distribution, inclusive of both bounds, swapping them if given out of order.
imports.reason: Distribution kept, entropy source replaced, as above.

imports.observed: A creature regains one block per 1000 ms, capped at 2, and spends one per blocked hit.
imports.reason: At 2000 ms between swings, 2 blocks regenerate per interval against a cap of 2, so a block is always available and the counter can never bind. A faster attacker would need it modelled; this phase has none.

imports.observed: Death-loss reduction counts blessings 2 through 8 — SEVEN regular blessings. Twist of Fate (1) is not one of them; it is the PvP skull protection.
Each regular blessing is worth 8 percentage points of reduction on a non-retro server.
Below level 24 the base loss is a flat 10 percent of total experience, not the level formula.

Below level 24, a blessing reduction of 40 percent or more is REPLACED by a flat 50 percent — before Promotion is added. Five, six and seven blessings therefore all reduce by the same 50 percent at low level.
From level 24 the base loss is a function of the fractional level and the total experience, which makes the ABSOLUTE experience lost depend on level alone.
Promotion adds 30 percentage points of reduction, AFTER the blessing handling and after the low-level replacement.
The result is a FRACTION of total experience: the base loss percent scaled by what the reductions left, divided by 100.
Experience lost is rounded UP. A death that would cost a fraction of a point costs a whole one.
Experience is only subtracted when the Character has NO vocation, or is above level 7. A vocationed Character at level 7 or below loses nothing.
imports.reason: Global Idle's Origin Character is vocation-less until the Level-8 Oracle, so it is on the FIRST side of this guard: it loses experience at every level. Recorded because reading only the 'level > 7' half would make the Origin Character immune to its own death penalty.

imports.observed: After the loss, the level is walked down while the remaining experience is below the level's requirement. Level 1 is the floor.
The unfair-fight reduction is 100 (a multiplier of 1.0) for every death that is not PvP against higher levels.
imports.reason: Phase 2 has no PvP, so the multiplier is always 1.0 and is not modelled as an input. The seam is the death policy's own parameters; PvP attaches there when it exists.

imports.observed: The configuration override is disabled by default, so the formula branch above is the live one.
A Character is promoted when its vocation has no further promotion AND is not itself the unpromoted entry — which is FALSE for a vocation-less Character.
The promoted vocation of a vocation id is the one whose fromVocation names it. Nothing names vocation 0, so vocation 0 has no promotion and is therefore not promoted.
imports.fixture: DL10 — a pre-vocation Character receives no Promotion reduction

imports.observed: Progress into the current level, as a percentage with two decimals; it feeds the fractional level the >= 24 formula uses.
Skill tries lost are TRUNCATED, not rounded up — the opposite of the experience loss in the same function.
imports.fixture: recorded only; Phase 4 owns durable Skills
imports.reason: Phase 2 has no durable Skill representation, and inventing one to delete it would be a shadow system. The rounding is recorded now so the phase that owns Skills does not re-derive it — and so the difference from the experience path is not mistaken for a transcription error later.

imports.observed: Eight blessings. Twist of Fate is 1; the seven that reduce death loss are 2 through 8.

A Rat drops exactly one cheese on 39410/100000 of kills, and the entry carries no maxCount, so the quantity is 1.
The Rat’s ENTIRE loot table is two entries: gold coin and cheese. There is no third drop to find.

Stackability is NOT in items.xml. It comes from the client appearance protobuf flag `cumulative`, which is why this record carries appearance probes.
The engine’s DEFAULT stack size is 100, and no item in data/items/items.xml overrides it.
imports.reason: The Product Owner locked maxStack 255 for an ordinary stackable. 255 is not invented: it is the ceiling this engine’s own parser enforces (item.stack.ceiling), so the override stays inside the source’s range. Recorded here so the divergence is visible rather than assumed.

imports.observed: The engine clamps any authored stack size to 255 and says so: "Stack size must be between 1 and 255."
A stackable item weighs its base weight TIMES its count; a non-stackable weighs its base weight once.
A vocation-less Character gains 10 oz of Capacity per level.
Capacity is stored in whole ounces and used in HUNDREDTHS, the same unit item weights are authored in.

imports.symbol: players sample 'Rook Sample' → level, vocation, cap
imports.observed: The sample Rookgaard character is level 2, vocation 0, cap 410. One gaincap of 10 below it puts a LEVEL 1 vocation-less Character at 400 oz — which is also the engine’s member default of 40000 hundredths.
The engine’s in-memory default Capacity is 40000 hundredths = 400.00 oz, which agrees with the level-1 arithmetic above.
The equipment slot vocabulary: HEAD 1, NECKLACE 2, BACKPACK 3, ARMOR 4, RIGHT 5, LEFT 6, LEGS 7, FEET 8, RING 9, AMMO 10.
imports.reason: Phase 3 implements HEAD, ARMOR, LEGS, FEET, LEFT (weapon hand) and BACKPACK — the slots the tutorial actually uses. The rest are imported as vocabulary so a later amulet or ring needs no schema change. STORE_INBOX has no Global Idle meaning and is not imported.

imports.observed: The source’s loot pouch is a 20-space container.
imports.reason: Global Idle takes the SHAPE, not the name: the name "Gold Pouch" is already the currency custody scope (ADR-019), so the physical one is the Loot Pouch. It is a per-Character custody rather than an item, and 20 is config-driven because the brief leaves the long-term count open.

imports.observed: The engine carries a server-configurable ceiling of 2000 on the loot pouch.
imports.fixture: recorded; the Phase 3 limit is the 20 spaces
imports.reason: Phase 3’s Loot Pouch is bounded by its spaces, which is the binding constraint at 20 spaces x 255 per stack. The 2000 is recorded so a later phase does not rediscover it.

imports.observed: The source resolves the loot pouch by looking for ITEM_GOLD_POUCH in the inventory, i.e. it is an ordinary container item.
imports.fixture: lootPouch is a CUSTODY, not an item
imports.reason: Global Idle’s Loot Pouch cannot be moved, equipped, dropped or manually filled, so modelling it as an item in a slot would create five illegal states the server would then have to forbid. It is a custody instead.
